name: Visa outlook
description: The owner's personal F-1 OPT / H-1B job-search view. Private: not shared publicly. Mirrors v_job_visa_outlook and python -m src.visa.scan.

cards.text:
## Visa outlook (private)
**Sources:** `v_job_visa_outlook` (posting signals + employer LCA history + cap-exempt hint) and `v_employer_sponsorship` (DOL LCA filings, last 3 loaded fiscal years).

**Mirrors:** `python -m src.visa.scan` and src/visa/README.md. Buckets apply in order: closed > strong > possible > unknown. Data window: see the right.

cards.title: Data window
cards.description: First and last UTC snapshot date in the database and the n behind this dashboard (in-scope jobs classified, and how many matched an LCA employer).

cards.title: Jobs per bucket
cards.description: In-scope jobs per bucket. unknown is not 'no': on truncated text a sponsorship sentence may have been cut off, and many employers simply have no LCA match.

cards.title: Strong and possible jobs
cards.description: Company, metro (the tracked-metro allowlist; instrument-limited), the rule that set the bucket, employer LCA counts and the posting URL. Read the full posting before applying.

cards.title: Employer sponsorship history (last 3 FYs)
cards.description: Employer-level aggregates of LCA filings: certified H-1B, new employment, analytics SOC, wage-level mix, median offered wage. A filing is not an approval or a hire.

cards.text:
**What this can't tell you** (src/visa/README.md)
- An LCA is not an approval or a hire.
- Counts favour large filers, staffing firms included.
- Truncated text hides signals: none_found on truncated text means unknown, never 'sponsors'.
- Cap-exempt is only a hint, from the company name alone.
- E-Verify (required for STEM OPT) isn't covered.
- Rules change: check with your school's DSO.
